classification.difficultyReason: Two journeys interchange running and walking speeds, requiring two linked time equations.

content.prompt: Raj runs at a speed of 6 metres per second and walks at a speed of 3 metres per second. Raj runs from his house to the post office then walks from the post office to work. This takes him 10 minutes. On the way home, he runs from work to the post office, then walks home. This takes him 8 minutes. How far is it from his house to the post office, and from the post office to his work?

answer.short:
House to post office: $720\text{ m}$. Post office to work: $1440\text{ m}$.

Use $t=\frac{d}{s}$ for each stage of both journeys and solve the two time equations.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ metres be the distance from the house to the post office and $y$ metres the distance from the post office to work. Each journey time is the sum of its two stage times.

$$\begin{align*}
\frac{x}{6}+\frac{y}{3}&=600\\
x+2y&=3600\\
\frac{x}{3}+\frac{y}{6}&=480\\
2x+y&=2880\\
3x+3y&=6480\\
x+y&=2160\\
y&=3600-2160\\
y&=1440\\
x&=2160-1440\\
x&=720
\end{align*}$$

The house is $720\text{ m}$ from the post office, and the post office is $1440\text{ m}$ from work.
